S78.01.needs: a Free account and a paid account, to compare
S78.01.note: The resolver itself has no screen. Its effect is seen only in the picker rows. Server-side checks are not visible in the UI.
steps: Sign in to AGI Cloud in the VS Code extension
Press Cmd+Shift+M, or run "Code: Select Model" from the Command Palette
Look at which rows are usable and which show a lock icon, then compare with the plan on the account
Expected: the list matches the plan and route the session resolved
S78.01.where: Code: Select Model (Cmd+Shift+M) shows the combined result of plan, model and route; locked rows show a lock icon

S78.02.needs: a signed-in account with at least two models that differ in effort support
S78.02.note: Attachment options per model were not located as a separate control. The only model-based attachment wording found is "cannot read images you attach" in modelConstants.ts. The sidebar view name was not verified.
steps: Open the chat composer
Note the "Mode and reasoning effort" button and its label
Press Cmd+Shift+M, or run "Code: Select Model", and choose a different model
Look at the model pill and the "Mode and reasoning effort" button: effort should appear, change or show "effort unavailable for this model" to match Expected
S78.02.where: The composer button titled "Mode and reasoning effort" (its summary shows the mode and effort), then pick a model in Code: Select Model (Cmd+Shift+M)

labels.text: This model does not take a reasoning effort.

S78.04.needs: a signed-in account with one model that takes effort and one that does not
S78.04.note: Whether unsupported levels are dropped from the request was only checked in the code, through supportedEffort in modelConstants.ts. The tester can see only what the menu offers.
steps: Pick a model that supports effort in Code: Select Model (Cmd+Shift+M)
Open the "Mode and reasoning effort" button and note the levels offered
Pick a model that does not take effort
Open the same button: it should read "This model does not take a reasoning effort." and no unsupported level should be sent, as Expected says
S78.04.where: The "Mode and reasoning effort" composer button, then the effort list after choosing a model

S78.07.note: The server-side check is not visible to a tester. Only the UI gate can be seen.
steps: Sign in with a Free account
Press Cmd+Shift+M, or run "Code: Select Model"
Choose a row with a lock icon
Expected: the message "is not in the plan this session resolved. Upgrade your AGI plan to use it." appears and no turn starts
S78.07.where: Locked rows in Code: Select Model (Cmd+Shift+M). The entitlement check runs in the app for each model and on the server for each route

S78.08.note: The rules that decide when the meter is shown were not traced. The pill and the list are the visible part.
steps: Sign in to an AGI Cloud account
Find the "Usage" pill in the chat panel
Click it to show usage details
Compare the remaining allowance and per-limit list with the server's numbers on the account's usage page
S78.08.where: The "Usage" pill in the chat panel (expand it to see "Per-limit usage breakdown")

labels.text: Code: Check the CLI in This Environment

S78.15.note: Whether the check command shows the localRuntimeClient message in the UI was not traced.

Run "Code: Check the CLI in This Environment"
Read the result message
Optional: set the agiWorkforce.cliPath setting to a path that does not exist, run the check again, and read the message "The AGI CLI could not be started." to compare with Expected

S78.17.needs: a signed-in account with a model that takes no effort
S78.17.note: The hidden-control rule is inside the webview. The visible part is the wording on the pill.
steps: Choose a model without reasoning effort in Code: Select Model (Cmd+Shift+M)
Hover the model pill
Expected: the effort part of the pill and its tooltip are absent or say "effort unavailable" instead of a broken control
S78.17.where: The model pill tooltip on the composer, which reads "effort unavailable for this model" when the model has no effort control

S78.18.note: The sentence shown on choosing a locked row was read in code, not seen in the UI.
steps: Sign in with a Free account
Press Cmd+Shift+M, or run "Code: Select Model"
Look for rows with a lock icon: they stay in the list but are disabled
Choose a locked row and read the reason that appears, as Expected says
S78.18.where: Code: Select Model (Cmd+Shift+M) > a locked row, shown with a lock icon and disabled

S78.19.note: The plan name in a locked row comes from the picker capability label. The paywall actions in cloudUtilityErrorActions.ts were not triggered.
steps: Sign in with a Free account
Press Cmd+Shift+M, choose a locked row, and read which plan it names (for example "Max plan")
Close the picker and click the "Upgrade" button in the chat panel, or run "Code: Upgrade Your Plan"
Expected: the plan that unlocks the feature and the way to upgrade are shown
S78.19.where: Code: Select Model (Cmd+Shift+M) > a locked row, or the "Upgrade" button in the chat panel, or Command Palette > "Code: Upgrade Your Plan"

S78.21.needs: a folder open in VS Code
S78.21.note: The visible label for the Bypass option was not found as plain text outside the tests. It likely comes from a mode label constant that was not traced.
steps: Open a folder in VS Code
Run "Code: Set Agent Mode" from the Command Palette
Choose the Bypass option
Read the warning "Turn on Bypass Permissions?" and its detail text, then press Cancel to compare with Expected
S78.21.where: Command Palette > "Code: Set Agent Mode", then choose Bypass

S78.22.needs: a condition that makes a turn fail, such as a Free account whose allowance is spent
S78.22.note: The failure button text "Switch model" was found in tests and in errorPresentation.ts logic, not verbatim in the source. The listed label is the picker entry.
steps: Choose a model and send a message that fails (for example, a model at its rate limit)
Read the failure message in the chat
Click the "Switch model" action
Expected: the model picker opens so another model can be chosen
S78.22.where: A chat turn that fails with provider unavailable, rate limit, spent free allowance, stream interrupted or safety refusal shows a "Switch model" action

S78.23.needs: an AGI Cloud account and a cloud task
S78.23.note: The when-clause that decides when the command appears was not checked. Pulling a cloud result back is a separate command, Code: Pull Cloud Task Into Workspace.
steps: Sign in to AGI Cloud and have a cloud task on a repository
Open the Command Palette and run "Code: Continue in the Cloud"
Read the result: the branch should be handed to a cloud session
Expected: the work continues in the other app or device
S78.23.where: Command Palette > "Code: Continue in the Cloud"

S78.24.needs: a signed-in account and a provider key

S78.26.needs: a signed-in account with two models that have different effort ladders
S78.26.note: The correction happens in supportedEffort in modelConstants.ts. The request itself is not visible in the UI, so only the button label can be compared.
steps: Choose a model with fewer effort levels in Code: Select Model (Cmd+Shift+M)
Set the effort to the highest level in the "Mode and reasoning effort" button
Send a short message
Expected: the effort sent is moved to the nearest level the model accepts, and the button shows that level
S78.26.where: The "Mode and reasoning effort" composer button, after changing model

S78.28.needs: a second account or plan change to test with
S78.28.note: The revalidation listener is in tierRevalidation.ts. What triggers the revalidation was not traced.
steps: Open Code: Select Model (Cmd+Shift+M) and note the lock icons
Change the plan on the account (outside VS Code)
Return to VS Code and open Code: Select Model again without restarting
Expected: the locked rows update to match the new plan
S78.28.where: Code: Select Model (Cmd+Shift+M) rows change after a plan change, without restarting VS Code
